clinician.trajectory_summary: A healthy 3-year-old girl presented with right-sided cheek and eye swelling and pain, and green nasal discharge. Initial treatment with oral antibiotics for suspected periorbital cellulitis was ineffective. Examination revealed diffuse erythematous swelling around the right cheek, jawline, and eye. Cranial imaging demonstrated a large central but predominantly right-sided nasopharyngeal tumor, extending into the ethmoid sinuses, orbits, infratemporal fossa, pterygoid muscles, and anterior and middle cranial fossae, with accompanying skull base destruction. Subsequent biopsy and staging confirmed the diagnosis of non-metastatic parameningeal rhabdomyosarcoma (PM-RMS).
